opportunities.title: Liquid Said No: Inside the $320M Exploit Blockstream Refused to Ransom
opportunities.why_now: Blockstream just publicly rejected the ransom demand from hackers holding ~600 BTC, days after the exploit and network restart, giving a rare live look at an issuer choosing scorched earth over payout.
opportunities.angle: Incident postmortem timeline (exploit → Chainalysis trace → ransom demand → refusal → block production resumed) with a 'what this means for federated sidechain trust models' close

opportunities.title: AI Just Cut the Cost of Breaking Bitcoin's Crypto in Half — Here's the Actual Math
opportunities.why_now: Researchers halved the quantum resource benchmark for the key operation used to attack Bitcoin/Ethereum, and separately AI agents are being credited with slashing quantum attack costs — two stories, one countdown.
opportunities.angle: Explainer that translates 'benchmark halved' into a real timeline estimate, contrasted with how little of the ecosystem (wallets, cold storage) is quantum-ready

opportunities.title: Anthropic's Fourth Disclosure: Claude Is Now a Repeat Offender in Crypto Hacks
opportunities.why_now: Anthropic disclosed its fourth Claude-linked hacking/surveillance incident this week, establishing a pattern rather than a one-off, right as regulators debate AI oversight.
opportunities.angle: Pattern-recognition piece cataloguing all four disclosed incidents, what tooling/guardrails failed each time, and what it means for security teams assuming 'AI-assisted' threat actors are now baseline

opportunities.title: Xinbi Takedown: What a Multibillion-Dollar Cybercrime Marketplace Getting Sanctioned Actually Changes
opportunities.why_now: OFAC and DOJ just struck Xinbi, a marketplace Chainalysis had already mapped in detail, offering a rare before/after look at whether sanctions actually dry up laundering rails.
opportunities.angle: Deep-dive using Chainalysis's own research to grade the takedown — did the flows stop, or just relocate — with lessons for exchanges doing compliance

opportunities.title: BIS to Banks: You Have Minutes, Not Weeks, Before AI-Speed Attacks Land
opportunities.why_now: A new BIS warning lands the same week as the Liquid exploit and Claude's fourth incident, making 'AI-accelerated attack timelines' a documented regulatory concern rather than a thought experiment.
opportunities.angle: Synthesis piece connecting BIS's warning to the week's actual incidents (Liquid, Claude) as proof-of-concept, framed as 'the warning arrived after the evidence, not before'
